chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
'Four [categories of heirs] — no harm shall be imposed on them with regards to the inheritance: the two parents, the husband, and the wife.'

key_terms.الزَّوْجُ: the husband — male spouse of the deceased
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the wife — female spouse of the deceased
key_terms.الْمِيرَاثُ: inheritance (mirath) — the Islamic law of succession dividing the deceased's estate among heirs
key_terms.الْوَالِدَانِ: the two parents — both father and mother, who are heirs in all circumstances
key_terms.ضَرَرٌ: harm/reduction (darar) — here referring specifically to reduction or shortfall in one's designated inheritance share

ai.seo_question: Which four heirs are protected from having their inheritance shares reduced in Islamic law according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) declares that four categories of heirs — both parents, the husband, and the wife — enjoy protected shares in Islamic inheritance law that cannot be diminished regardless of other heirs present. This ruling addresses the principle of 'awl (proportional reduction of shares when total exceeds the estate), affirming that these four are exempt from any reduction. In the context of early Islamic jurisprudence, this teaching would have clarified for jurists and ordinary believers the inviolable nature of these inheritance shares against competing claims.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, from Abu Baseer from, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘Four’, no harm is entered upon them with regards to the inheritance – the two parents, and the husband, and the wife’.
en.sarwar: 2. Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from abu al-Mighra’ from Ibrahim ibn Maymun from Salim al-Ashal who has narrated the following: “He had heard abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has placed the parents with all other heirs and [nothing] from their one-sixth is reduced.
He has placed husband and wife with heirs and [nothing] is reduced from one-fourth and one-eighth.’”
